description: Prosody as a medium-INDEPENDENT channel of communicative FUNCTION — how a thing is said, carrying meaning the words alone don't. The functions here are realized differently per medium (acoustically as F0/timing/loudness in speech; orthographically as punctuation/caps/emphasis/elongation/asides in text — the text_prosody expansion pack) but the function is the same. The renderer/W_j principle applied to delivery: one prosodic intent, many surface forms. Each function is ALREADY example-grounded in the TV Tropes corpus by named conventions (its exemplar_tropes), which the TropesTeacher serves on demand — so grounding flows from the corpus, not from hand-coded rules. Prosody is also the EVIDENCE the comprehension frames consume: delivery_contradicts_content is what fires the irony frame.

concepts.name: emphasis
concepts.definition: Prominence placed on an element to mark it as important or stressed. Acoustically a pitch accent + extra duration/loudness; orthographically italics, caps, or punctuated-for-emphasis. The element made prominent is the one the speaker wants weighted.

concepts.name: focus
concepts.definition: Information structure: which part of an utterance is foregrounded as new or contrastive vs background/given. 'I didn't say HE stole it' focuses 'he' — the stress placement changes what is contradicted. Prosody marks focus directly; getting focus wrong changes the meaning.

concepts.name: sentence_type
concepts.definition: Whether an utterance is a statement, question, or command — carried by delivery (rising vs falling contour) or orthography (?, ., !) as much as by syntax. The contour can override the words: a statement said with rising intonation becomes a question.

concepts.name: affect
concepts.definition: The speaker's emotional state carried in delivery — the principal channel for emotion in speech. Loud+high+fast reads as excited/angry; quiet+low+slow as sad/calm. Reading affect from a partner's delivery is the entry point to theory-of-mind; the agent's own emotion nodes shape its delivery when it speaks.

concepts.name: stance
concepts.definition: The speaker's attitude toward the content and the listener — register, formality, politeness, distance. Carried by word choice and delivery together; a register mismatch (sophisticated words, crude delivery, or vice versa) is itself meaningful.

concepts.name: pacing
concepts.definition: Rhythm, timing, and pause as meaning. A held pause creates suspense or weight; a beat lands a joke; rushing signals urgency. Silence is a prosodic act — the absence is the signal.

concepts.name: turn_management
concepts.definition: Delivery cues that manage the exchange: a falling final contour yields the turn, a sustained one holds it, an overlap interrupts. How speakers negotiate who talks when without saying so.

concepts.name: delivery_contradicts_content
concepts.definition: The keystone: delivery signals the OPPOSITE of (or something other than) what the words literally say — flat affect on a compliment, sweet tone on a threat. This is the acoustic/orthographic evidence that fires the irony/sarcasm frame (figurative Mt). Without this channel, sincere and sarcastic 'nice job' are indistinguishable.

concepts.name: idiolect
concepts.definition: Stable individual delivery markers that identify a speaker — verbal tics, catchphrases, characteristic rhythm. Carries identity rather than propositional content; recognising it is part of modelling WHO is speaking.

wiring_note: Prosody is wired UP into the substrate's perceptual + linguistic foundations. audio_psychoacoustics is the perceptual layer where prosodic features (pitch, duration, loudness) are heard. audio_music_perception shares the rhythm + meter primitives prosody uses (research from Patel and others on the rhythm-music-language overlap). language_foundation gives the linguistic encoding prosody serves. Together: prosody is what the auditory system perceives + what the linguistic system encodes.
